chapters.title: In the Beginning Was the Word
chapters.synopsis: John declares that the Word was with God and was God, and that this Word became flesh and dwelt among mortals full of grace and truth. John the Baptist testifies that he is not the Christ but the voice preparing the way, and points his own disciples to the Lamb of God. Andrew, Peter, Philip, and others leave their nets and their doubts to follow Jesus.

segments.note: The Word was God and became flesh

chapters.title: Water into Wine
chapters.synopsis: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine at his mother's request, the first of his miracles, and his disciples believe on him. He goes down briefly to Capernaum, then up to Jerusalem for the passover, where he drives the moneychangers from the temple and speaks of raising up its destroyed temple in three days.

chapters.title: Ye Must Be Born Again
chapters.synopsis: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night, and Jesus teaches that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again of water and of the Spirit. He declares that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth should not perish. John the Baptist rejoices that the bridegroom's voice has come, saying he must increase while I must decrease.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: Born again; God so loved the world

chapters.title: The Water of Life at the Well
chapters.synopsis: Weary at Jacob's well in Samaria, Jesus asks a woman for water and offers her living water that becomes a well springing up unto everlasting life. She recognizes him as a prophet and then hurries to tell the city, and many Samaritans believe on his word. Returning to Galilee, Jesus heals a nobleman's son at Capernaum with only a word, though he is absent from the boy's bedside.

chapters.title: Take Up Thy Bed and Walk
chapters.synopsis: At the pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus heals a man who had been infirm thirty-eight years and bids him take up his bed and walk, though it is the sabbath day. When the Jews seek to kill him for this and for calling God his Father, Jesus testifies that the Father has committed all judgment to the Son and that the dead in the graves shall hear his voice.

chapters.title: I Am the Bread of Life
chapters.synopsis: Jesus feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fishes, then walks upon the sea to his disciples in the storm. When the multitude seeks him again, he teaches that he is the bread of life come down from heaven, and that whoso eateth his flesh and drinketh his blood hath eternal life. Many disciples are offended and walk no more with him, but Peter testifies that he has the words of eternal life.

chapters.title: Never Man Spake Like This Man
chapters.synopsis: At the feast of tabernacles Jesus goes up to Jerusalem secretly and then teaches openly in the temple, declaring that his doctrine is not his own but the Father's who sent him. On the last great day of the feast he cries that whoever thirsts may come to him and drink, and the officers sent to take him return amazed, saying never man spake like this man.

chapters.title: Before Abraham Was, I Am
chapters.synopsis: Jesus forgives a woman taken in adultery, telling her accusers that he who is without sin should cast the first stone, and bids her sin no more. He declares himself the light of the world and that the truth shall make his followers free, and when the Jews boast of Abraham, he answers that before Abraham was, I am, at which they take up stones to stone him.

chapters.title: One Thing I Know: I Was Blind
chapters.synopsis: Jesus anoints the eyes of a man blind from birth with clay and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, and he comes away seeing. The Pharisees, troubled that this was done on the sabbath, question the man and his parents and cast him out of the synagogue for confessing Christ. Jesus finds him again and opens his eyes further to see the Son of God, while those who claim to see remain blind in their sin.

chapters.title: I Am the Good Shepherd
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches that he is the good shepherd who calls his own sheep by name and lays down his life for them, unlike the hireling who flees. He has other sheep not of this fold that he must also bring. At the feast of dedication he declares that he and the Father are one, and when the Jews take up stones, he escapes out of their hand.

chapters.title: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
chapters.synopsis: Word comes that Lazarus is sick, but Jesus tarries until he has died, then comes to Bethany where Martha meets him and hears his testimony that he is the resurrection and the life. Jesus weeps, then calls Lazarus forth from the tomb four days dead, and many believe. The chief priests and Pharisees, alarmed, take counsel from that day to put Jesus to death.

chapters.title: A Corn of Wheat Must Die
chapters.synopsis: At Bethany a woman anoints Jesus's feet with costly ointment against the day of his burial, and the next day the multitudes hail him with palms as he enters Jerusalem. When Greeks seek him out, Jesus teaches that a corn of wheat must fall into the ground and die to bring forth fruit, foretelling his own coming death. Though he has done many miracles, many still do not believe on him.

chapters.title: A New Commandment I Give unto You
chapters.synopsis: At supper Jesus rises, girds himself with a towel, and washes his disciples' feet as an example of humble service. He foretells that one of the twelve will betray him, and after Judas goes out into the night, Jesus gives a new commandment: that they love one another as he has loved them. He also foretells that Peter will deny him three times before the cock crows.

chapters.title: I Am the Way, the Truth, and the Life
chapters.synopsis: Jesus comforts his troubled disciples with the promise of many mansions in his Father's house and declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father but by him. He promises another Comforter, the Holy Ghost, who will teach them all things, and leaves them his peace, not as the world gives.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: The way, the truth, the life; the Comforter promised

chapters.title: I Am the Vine, Ye Are the Branches
chapters.synopsis: Jesus teaches that he is the true vine and his disciples are the branches, and that apart from him they can do nothing. He commands them to abide in his love and to love one another as he has loved them, laying down his life for his friends. He warns that the world will hate them as it hated him, for a servant is not greater than his lord.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: The vine and the branches; love one another

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: The world will hate you as it hated me

chapters.title: Be of Good Cheer
chapters.synopsis: Jesus warns his disciples that they will be put out of the synagogues and even killed, but promises that the Comforter will come and guide them into all truth. He tells them their sorrow at his going will be turned to joy, like a woman forgetting her travail for joy that a child is born, and bids them be of good cheer, for he has overcome the world.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: Sorrow turned to joy; I have overcome the world

chapters.title: The Intercessory Prayer
chapters.synopsis: Lifting his eyes to heaven, Jesus prays to the Father that the hour has come to glorify the Son, and defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent. He prays not for the world but for those the Father has given him, and for all who will believe on him through their word, that they may be one even as he and the Father are one.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: The intercessory prayer for his disciples and all believers

chapters.title: The Betrayal and the Denial
chapters.synopsis: In a garden across the Kidron, Jesus is betrayed by Judas and arrested, and Peter cuts off a servant's ear before Jesus bids him put up his sword. Led first to Annas and then to Caiaphas, Jesus is questioned while Peter, warming himself in the courtyard, denies him three times before the cock crows. At daybreak he is delivered to Pilate, who finds in him no fault at all.

chapters.title: It Is Finished
chapters.synopsis: Pilate scourges Jesus and presents him crowned with thorns, but yields to the crowd's demand and delivers him to be crucified. On the cross Jesus commits his mother to the beloved disciple's care, and after crying that it is finished, bows his head and gives up the ghost. A soldier pierces his side, and Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus lay his body in a new tomb.

chapters.title: My Lord and My God
chapters.synopsis: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and weeps until the risen Jesus calls her by name. That evening he appears to the gathered disciples and breathes on them the Holy Ghost, but Thomas, absent, refuses to believe without seeing. Eight days later Jesus invites Thomas to touch his wounds, and Thomas answers, my Lord and my God, that those who have not seen and yet believe may be blessed.

chapters.title: Feed My Sheep
chapters.synopsis: By the sea of Galilee the risen Jesus fills the disciples' empty nets with a miraculous catch, and Peter swims ashore to him while the others follow in the ship. After they dine together, Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him and charges him each time to feed his sheep, then foretells the manner of Peter's death and bids him, follow me.
